candidate.title: TCR Chain / Paring
candidate.scope: The middle row labeled TCR Chain / Paring: an oil-emulsion, overlap-extension architecture for identifying T-cell receptor α–β chain pairing in single cells, ending in DNA with linked CDR3α and CDR3β regions. Preserve Paring as drawn; the registered parent poster bibliography spells its corresponding entry TCR Chain Pairing and cites Turchaninova M. A. et al. (2013), Eur J Immunol 43:2507–2515. This identifies a particular catalogue-associated implementation, not all TCR-pairing assays. The neighboring STRT row above and TCR-LA-MC PCR row below have independent routes and are outside scope. The oil-emulsion enclosure spans reverse transcription, amplification and overlap extension. Blocker primers enter the downstream PCR stage, which depicts linked-product amplification and non-fused-product suppression as distinct outcomes; no arrow establishes serial transfer between those two substrate/product drawings. The declared scope is the depicted architecture, without unshown adapter addition, sequencing execution or complete experimental implementation.

unknowns.question: Which registered publication-text source ID can encode the verified association of TCR Chain Paring with Turchaninova et al., Pairing of T-cell receptor chains via emulsion PCR, PMID 23696157, DOI 10.1002/eji.201343453? The parent poster reference was directly inspected and matches the journal, year, volume and pages. An additional independent lookup inspected https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23696157/ (bibliographic metadata and primary abstract, especially Abstract) and https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/eji.201343453 (publisher identity, Abstract and the displayed Supporting Information description). The primary abstract was checked, not merely a title or PMID. The publisher full-text link redirected to its abstract; full-text chemistry was not verified. The supplied immutable registry contains only catalogue card and diagram entries, with no metadata/abstract/fulltext publication source. The validator requires such a registered text source for every PaperMatch, so neither treating the image as a primary paper nor inventing an unregistered source ID would be valid. publication_source_entry.json preserves the bounded verified identity/abstract excerpt as a proposed entry for caller registration; it has not been inserted into the read-only registry. This is a blocking provenance/interface gap for the required PaperMatch, not an unknown paper identity or a missing experimental step, and does not block the schematic-level architecture. Registration of the checked abstract/metadata is sufficient; full text is not needed for the currently asserted architecture.
